minutes.headline: Board appointed Sue Doherty Council on Aging director and declined to buy Chapter 61 land on White Street.
minutes.summary: The Select Board appointed a new Council on Aging director on the screening committee's recommendation. It declined to exercise its right of first refusal on Chapter 61 land at White Street. It reviewed testimony for the Unitil rate hearing and designated election officials as special municipal employees. Committee reports included a school budget update with Title I grant news.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to appoint a new Council on Aging director on the town manager's and screening committee's recommendation.
The board took up whether to use the town's right of first refusal on 11 acres of Chapter 61 land on White Street; the outcome was not audible in the recording.
The board voted on designating election officials as special municipal employees; the outcome was not audible in the recording.
The board reviewed draft testimony for the Unitil rate hearing at the state Department of Public Utilities.
A school update said a larger Title I grant would pay for two reading specialists, and that extra Chapter 70 revenue could not go to schools without a special town meeting vote.

why_it_matters: The Chapter 61 decision decides whether the town gave up a chance to buy open land or let it move to a private sale, and the recording does not make the result clear.
Extra state school aid that needs a special town meeting vote before it reaches schools is a vote residents may be asked to take, and the Title I grant adds school staff without a local tax cost.
